Oskar is not introduced. His role and the context of the question are unknown.

stumbles.quote: A lookup table that uses only the hit's lint category—its historical tic rate—reached AUROC 0.769.
stumbles.why: 'Historical' is unexplained. The table may have been built from the same 261 hits it was evaluated on, which would leak test data. The text doesn't say.

stumbles.quote: The category rate carries most of the signal because individual `declaude_lint` rules sit near the extremes of precision.
stumbles.why: The text treats 'lint category' and 'rule' as the same thing without saying so. Its evidence (triad 5/44 and participle 5/43) is not near an extreme to the same degree as negation-first 16/18, and this isn't explained.

point: A small calibrated classifier, Jev, was weak at filtering false alarms from regex style lints on LLM prose. It settled only 24.5% of hits at a 5% error budget, and a simple per-rule tic-rate lookup did almost as well, so it was rejected.
